chess-lab

Eleven questions people repeat about chess, checked against 190,967 real games and Stockfish 16. One track exists only to break the others.

Read this before the findings

Three results below are nulls. A null is nearly content-free without a resolution bound attached, so here is what each design could actually have detected.

Clustering moves within games costs a 2.18x sample penalty for the same resolution, and every bound above carries it.

Two published claims have been withdrawn

"Save rate falls monotonically with rating." An artifact of truncating evaluation at ply 120, which preferentially discarded long defensive games. Every game is now scored to its end.

"Amateurs save by winning, masters save by drawing." The contrast disappears once each group is normalised by its own base draw rate. Caught by falsification probe P1, which still fires.

Both retractions are pinned by tests, and the claims checker fails if the retraction text is removed while the probe still fires.

Findings

3Blunders, rating and thinking time

Blunder rate falls about 3.4x from 1200 to 2200. Faster games blunder roughly 29% more than slower ones, tested as a difference rather than by comparing interval overlap. Time control shifts the mean by a little; which two humans sat down shifts it by a lot.

5White's first-move advantage

White scores above parity in every over-the-board band, and the edge grows with strength rather than shrinking. Draw rates are falling, not rising, which is the opposite of the usual claim. The unrestricted version of that trend is a composition artifact and is published alongside it.

2Do engine-approved openings win more?

No, at any rating. Nothing survives multiplicity correction and the sign of the rank correlation flips between bands. The mechanical reason is range compression: every mainline opening evaluates within a 26 centipawn band.

4Rating inflation, at fixed nominal rating

No detectable drift. The design cannot separate inflation from a change in who holds a rating, and it is not powered to rule out the drift rate people actually claim.

8Rating inflation, following the same players

Null again, from a different direction. Player fixed effects remove the composition confound entirely, then run into the age-period-cohort problem: within a player, calendar year and career stage are the same regressor after demeaning.

9Saving lost positions, format held constant

No gradient across 400 Elo of over-the-board play. Combined with the online sample, both corpora are internally flat and separated by a large step, which points at playing format rather than strength.

11Is the save-rate gap skill, or is it format?

The deepest result here. Matching online and over-the-board players on engine-measured skill, rather than on rating scales that are not comparable across the two, does not shrink the gap: it widens it to 17.3 points. The mechanism is behavioural and measurable without conditioning on anything. Of players who ended up losing, 32.0% online played the position to checkmate against 5.8% over the board. A player who resigns forgoes any chance of saving the game, which explains the whole difference without invoking chess skill at all.

10Do the findings survive their own analytic choices?

Track 3's gradient is negative in all 180 defensible specifications and the reported choice sits at the 74th percentile. One arbitrary decision, the blunder threshold, drives 94% of the spread.

7The track that attacks the others

Six probes with pass conditions fixed in advance. One still fires, against track 6, and forced a published claim to be withdrawn. Two others record bugs that were real and are now fixed at the cause.

Reproduce or reuse

pip install -e ".[dev]"
apt-get install stockfish
make data      # ~150 MB from GitHub mirrors
make build     # ~1h, engine-bound, resumable
make verify    # tests + claims check + manifest check

The engine evaluations are the only expensive artifact here, roughly an hour of single-core Stockfish. chesslab export writes them as 125,673 scored moves joined to game metadata, with a data dictionary documenting four traps, three of which produced real errors during this build.

chesslab limits prints every known confound and resolution bound. If you think a finding is wrong, there is an issue template for exactly that: it is the contribution this project most wants.
